title: Wall-clock timing assertion is an inherently flaky acceptance test
evidence: test/queries.test.ts:170-177 asserts `Date.now() - t < 2000` for four aggregate queries; on a loaded runner this can fail with nothing broken
suggestion: Move the perf bound to a dedicated benchmark that reports rather than asserts, or drop the absolute threshold from the acceptance run

title: Acceptance tests call internal query functions directly instead of through the MCP protocol/DSL
evidence: test/queries.test.ts:47,66,72 call q.headToHead(ds,...), q.teamRecord(ds,...), q.rankTeams(ds,...) with the raw dataset singleton; only server.test.ts (1 test) exercises the real MCP tool surface
suggestion: Route acceptance cases through the MCP Client (already present in server.test.ts) behind a thin domain DSL so specs assert outcomes, not internal APIs

title: Tests pin exact magic counts tied to the current CSV fixtures
evidence: test/queries.test.ts:37 asserts ds.players.length === 18207 and :99 asserts [wins,draws,losses] === [28,6,4]; these break on any data-file change or SOCCER_DATA_DIR override
suggestion: Assert ranges or derived/known facts rather than exact fixture-dependent magic numbers

title: Several acceptance cases bundle multiple outcomes + structural invariants
evidence: test/queries.test.ts:47-52 (Q1) asserts the h2h string AND aWins+bWins+draws===matches.length AND matches.length>30 in one test
suggestion: Split data-structure invariants into unit tests; let each acceptance case assert a single domain outcome

title: Implementation exceeds the spec's required capability set
evidence: src/server.ts registers 18 tools incl. derbies, team_profile (cross-dataset join), player skill attributes and dataset_info beyond the 12 pinned requirements
suggestion: No action — noting coverage beyond spec for cross-run comparison
